description: Process medical billing and coding from encounter documentation through claim submission, tracking, and denial management.

steps.description: Receive and review encounter documentation for billing readiness.

inputs.name: encounter-notes
inputs.desc: Clinical documentation from the provider visit

inputs.name: patient-demographics
inputs.desc: Patient name, DOB, insurance, account number

outputs.name: encounter-summary
outputs.desc: Structured summary of the encounter including diagnoses and procedures performed

outputs.name: documentation-gaps
outputs.desc: List of missing or unclear documentation that needs provider clarification

process: Review the encounter notes for completeness (chief complaint, history, exam, assessment, plan).
Extract the diagnoses and procedures documented by the provider.
Flag any documentation gaps that would prevent accurate coding.
Return the encounter summary and any gaps requiring follow-up.

steps.description: Assign ICD-10 diagnosis codes and CPT/HCPCS procedure codes to the encounter.

outputs.name: coded-encounter
outputs.desc: Encounter with assigned ICD-10 and CPT/HCPCS codes, modifiers, and units

outputs.name: coding-notes
outputs.desc: Notes on code selection rationale and any queries sent to the provider

process: Select the ICD-10 codes that match the documented diagnoses, sequencing the primary diagnosis first.
Assign the CPT or HCPCS codes for each procedure, including modifiers and units.
Verify that the diagnosis codes support the medical necessity of each procedure code.
Document the coding rationale and any queries sent back to the provider for clarification.

steps.description: Verify the coded encounter for compliance with payer rules and coding guidelines.

outputs.name: compliant-encounter
outputs.desc: Encounter that has passed compliance checks

outputs.name: compliance-flags
outputs.desc: Any issues found during compliance review (bundling, modifier misuse, medical necessity)

process: Check for correct use of modifiers and code bundling rules (CCI edits).
Verify medical necessity by matching diagnosis codes to procedure codes against payer LCD/NCD policies.
Confirm that the E/M level matches the documented complexity.
Return the compliant encounter or flag issues for correction.

steps.description: Submit the coded claim to the payer through the clearinghouse.

outputs.name: submitted-claim
outputs.desc: Claim record with submission date, payer, and tracking number

outputs.name: submission-errors
outputs.desc: Any rejection errors from the clearinghouse

process: Build the claim (CMS-1500 or 837P) with the patient demographics, codes, and charges.
Submit the claim through the clearinghouse to the payer.
Record the submission date, tracking number, and payer.
Handle any clearinghouse rejections by correcting and resubmitting.

steps.description: Track the claim through the adjudication process and record the payer response.

outputs.name: adjudicated-claim
outputs.desc: Claim with payer decision (paid, denied, partial) and payment details

outputs.name: denial-list
outputs.desc: List of denied line items with denial reason codes

process: Check the claim status with the payer at defined intervals (7, 14, 30 days).
Record the ERA/EOB when received, including allowed amounts, adjustments, and patient responsibility.
Separate paid claims from denied or partially denied claims.
Pass denied items to the denial management step.

steps.description: Handle claim denials by analyzing the reason, correcting errors, and filing appeals.

inputs.name: denial-list
inputs.desc: Denied line items with reason codes

outputs.name: billing-record
outputs.desc: Final billing record with payment, adjustments, and appeal outcomes

outputs.name: denial-trends
outputs.desc: Summary of denial patterns for process improvement

process: Categorize each denial by reason (eligibility, authorization, coding, timely filing, medical necessity).
For correctable denials, fix the error and resubmit the claim.
For clinical denials, prepare and submit the appeal with supporting documentation.
Track appeal outcomes and summarize denial trends for process improvement.

description: Verify patient insurance eligibility and benefits before a visit, including copay estimation and prior authorization checks.

steps.description: Collect the patient's insurance information from their card and intake forms.

inputs.name: insurance-card-data
inputs.desc: Information from the insurance card (payer, plan, member ID, group number)

outputs.name: insurance-profile
outputs.desc: Structured insurance record with payer, plan, member ID, group, and effective dates

outputs.name: secondary-insurance
outputs.desc: Secondary insurance information if applicable

process: Record the primary insurance payer, plan name, member ID, and group number from the card.
Confirm the subscriber relationship (self, spouse, child, other).
Check for secondary insurance and record if present.
Verify that the information matches the practice management system.

steps.description: Verify eligibility and benefits with the payer electronically or by phone.

inputs.name: visit-type
inputs.desc: The type of visit or service planned (office visit, procedure, imaging)

outputs.name: eligibility-result
outputs.desc: Active or inactive status, effective dates, and plan type

outputs.name: benefits-detail
outputs.desc: Copay, coinsurance, deductible (met and remaining), out-of-pocket max, and visit limits

process: Submit the 270/271 eligibility inquiry to the payer electronically.
Record the coverage status (active, terminated, pending) and effective dates.
Extract the benefits for the planned visit type (copay, coinsurance percentage, deductible amounts).
Note any visit limits, referral requirements, or network restrictions.

steps.description: Determine whether the planned service requires prior authorization from the payer.

outputs.name: auth-requirement
outputs.desc: Whether prior authorization is required, and for which services

outputs.name: auth-instructions
outputs.desc: Instructions for obtaining authorization if required (phone, portal, form)

process: Check the benefits response for prior authorization requirements for the planned service.
Cross-reference with the payer's authorization list for the CPT code range.
If authorization is required, record the submission method and turnaround time.
Flag the visit for the prior authorization workflow if needed.

steps.description: Calculate and communicate the patient's estimated out-of-pocket cost for the visit.

outputs.name: cost-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated patient responsibility for the visit (copay, coinsurance, deductible applied)

outputs.name: verification-record
outputs.desc: Complete verification record for the patient chart

process: Calculate the expected charge based on the fee schedule for the visit type.
Apply the patient's copay, coinsurance, and remaining deductible to estimate out-of-pocket cost.
Prepare the cost estimate for communication to the patient before the visit.
File the complete verification record in the patient chart.

description: Manage patient referrals from receipt through scheduling, visit, and records return to the referring provider.

steps.description: Receive the referral and verify the authorization and patient information.

inputs.name: referral-document
inputs.desc: Referral order from the referring provider

outputs.name: verified-referral
outputs.desc: Referral with confirmed authorization, patient identity, and insurance eligibility

outputs.name: referral-issues
outputs.desc: Any problems with the referral (expired, wrong provider, missing info)

process: Verify the referring provider's information and the referral reason.
Confirm the referral authorization number and expiration date with the payer.
Verify the patient's identity and insurance eligibility for the referred service.
Flag any issues that need resolution before scheduling.

steps.description: Schedule the referred patient for the appropriate visit type.

outputs.name: scheduled-appointment
outputs.desc: Appointment date, time, provider, and location

outputs.name: pre-visit-packet
outputs.desc: Instructions and forms sent to the patient before the visit

process: Match the referral to the appropriate provider and visit type.
Schedule the appointment within the authorization timeframe.
Send the patient the appointment confirmation and pre-visit instructions.
Request relevant records from the referring provider.

steps.description: Complete the referral by sending records and a consult report back to the referring provider.

outputs.name: consult-report
outputs.desc: Report sent to the referring provider with findings and recommendations

outputs.name: referral-tracking-record
outputs.desc: Complete referral record from intake through closeout

process: After the visit, prepare the consult report with findings, diagnoses, and recommendations.
Send the consult report to the referring provider within the agreed timeframe.
Update the referral tracking record with the visit outcome and report sent date.
Close the referral in the tracking system.

description: Schedule clinic appointments by matching visit type to provider availability, verifying insurance, and managing the waitlist.

steps.description: Receive and categorize the scheduling request by visit type and urgency.

inputs.name: scheduling-request
inputs.desc: Patient's request for an appointment (phone, portal, in-person, referral)

inputs.name: patient-record
inputs.desc: Patient demographics and insurance on file

outputs.name: categorized-request
outputs.desc: Request categorized by visit type (new, follow-up, procedure, urgent) and urgency

outputs.name: scheduling-constraints
outputs.desc: Constraints on scheduling (specific provider, insurance network, authorization needed)

process: Determine the visit type from the patient's reason for the appointment.
Check urgency (routine, urgent, same-day).
Identify scheduling constraints (provider preference, insurance network, referral/authorization).
Verify the patient's insurance is active and in-network.

steps.description: Match the request to available provider time slots based on visit type and constraints.

outputs.name: offered-slots
outputs.desc: List of available appointment slots that meet the criteria

outputs.name: waitlist-option
outputs.desc: Waitlist position if no immediate slots are available

process: Search the scheduling system for open slots matching the visit type and provider.
Filter by insurance network and authorization status.
Offer the patient the earliest available slots.
If no slots are available within the target timeframe, offer a waitlist position.

steps.description: Book the appointment and send confirmation with pre-visit instructions.

inputs.name: offered-slots
inputs.desc: Available slots presented to the patient

outputs.name: booked-appointment
outputs.desc: Confirmed appointment with date, time, provider, location, and visit type

outputs.name: scheduling-record
outputs.desc: Complete scheduling record including waitlist management

process: Book the selected slot and update the provider's schedule.
Send the patient the appointment confirmation via their preferred channel (text, email, portal).
Include pre-visit instructions (forms, fasting, what to bring).
Set up the appointment reminder sequence (48 hours, 24 hours before).

description: Obtain prior authorization from an insurer for a medical service, from documentation gathering through approval and communication.

steps.description: Identify the services requiring prior authorization and the payer's submission requirements.

inputs.name: planned-services
inputs.desc: List of planned services or procedures with CPT codes

inputs.name: patient-insurance
inputs.desc: Patient's insurance plan and payer information

outputs.name: auth-requirements
outputs.desc: Which services need authorization, the payer's submission method, and required documentation

outputs.name: timeline
outputs.desc: Expected turnaround time and any urgency options

process: Cross-reference the planned CPT codes against the payer's authorization list.
Identify the payer's submission method (portal, fax, phone).
List the required clinical documentation for each service.
Note the standard and expedited turnaround times.

steps.description: Gather and organize the clinical documentation required for the authorization submission.

inputs.name: auth-requirements
inputs.desc: Required documentation list from the payer

outputs.name: auth-package
outputs.desc: Complete authorization submission package with clinical notes, test results, and payer forms

outputs.name: missing-items
outputs.desc: Any documentation still needed before submission

process: Pull the relevant clinical notes, imaging results, lab results, and referral from the patient record.
Complete the payer's authorization request form.
Write the clinical rationale or letter of medical necessity if required.
Verify the package is complete before submission.

steps.description: Submit the authorization request and track it through the payer's review process.

outputs.name: auth-status
outputs.desc: Current authorization status (submitted, in review, approved, denied, peer review requested)

outputs.name: auth-tracking-number
outputs.desc: Payer's reference number for the authorization request

process: Submit the authorization package through the payer's required channel.
Record the submission date, tracking number, and expected decision date.
Follow up with the payer if no response by the expected date.
Respond to any payer requests for additional information within 24 hours.

steps.description: Communicate the authorization decision to the patient and scheduling team, and handle denials.

outputs.name: authorization-record
outputs.desc: Complete authorization record with decision, dates, and any appeal outcome

outputs.name: scheduling-clearance
outputs.desc: Clearance for scheduling (approved) or hold notice (denied/pending appeal)

process: If approved, record the authorization number, approved services, and validity dates.
Notify the scheduling team to proceed with booking.
If denied, review the denial reason and decide whether to appeal or pursue alternatives.
Communicate the outcome to the patient, including any financial implications.

description: Collect patient balances after insurance adjudication through statements, reminders, payment plans, and escalation.

steps.description: Generate the patient statement after insurance has processed the claim.

inputs.name: adjudicated-claims
inputs.desc: Claims with insurance payment applied and remaining patient balance

inputs.name: patient-account
inputs.desc: Patient account information and contact details

outputs.name: patient-statement
outputs.desc: Itemized statement showing services, insurance payments, adjustments, and patient balance due

outputs.name: balance-summary
outputs.desc: Total balance due, age of charges, and payment due date

process: Calculate the patient responsibility from the ERA/EOB (copay, coinsurance, deductible, non-covered).
Generate the itemized statement with service dates, descriptions, and amounts.
Set the payment due date (typically 30 days from statement date).
Send the statement via the patient's preferred method (mail, email, portal).

steps.description: Send follow-up reminders and contact the patient about unpaid balances.

inputs.name: patient-account
inputs.desc: Patient contact details and payment history

outputs.name: follow-up-record
outputs.desc: Record of all collection contacts (dates, methods, responses)

outputs.name: payment-arrangement
outputs.desc: Payment plan or payment made, if any

process: Send the second statement at 30 days past due with a reminder notice.
Make a phone call at 60 days past due to discuss payment options.
Offer a payment plan for balances the patient cannot pay in full.
Send a final notice at 90 days warning of potential referral to collections.

steps.description: Escalate unresolved balances to an external collections agency or write off as bad debt.

outputs.name: collections-record
outputs.desc: Final disposition of the balance (paid, payment plan, sent to agency, written off)

outputs.name: collections-report
outputs.desc: Summary of collection outcomes for the billing cycle

process: Review the account for any remaining insurance follow-up before escalating.
For balances over the threshold and older than 120 days, refer to the collections agency.
For small balances below the collection threshold, write off as bad debt.
Record the final disposition and update the patient account.

description: Credential a healthcare provider with insurance payers, from document collection through approval and re-credentialing.

steps.description: Collect and verify the provider's credentialing documents.

inputs.name: provider-info
inputs.desc: Provider name, NPI, specialty, and practice affiliation

inputs.name: credentialing-checklist
inputs.desc: List of required documents by payer

outputs.name: provider-file
outputs.desc: Complete credentialing file with all required documents verified

outputs.name: document-gaps
outputs.desc: Any missing or expired documents that need to be obtained

process: Collect the provider's licenses, DEA certificate, board certifications, and malpractice insurance.
Verify education, training, and work history.
Obtain the malpractice claims history and any disciplinary actions.
Check the NPDB, OIG exclusion list, and state sanctions.

steps.description: Complete and maintain the provider's CAQH ProView profile.

outputs.name: caqh-profile
outputs.desc: Completed CAQH profile with attestation

outputs.name: caqh-id
outputs.desc: Provider's CAQH ID number

process: Create or update the CAQH ProView profile with all provider information.
Upload supporting documents (licenses, insurance, certifications).
Complete the attestation and authorize payer access.
Set the re-attestation reminder (every 120 days).

steps.description: Submit credentialing applications to each insurance payer.

outputs.name: enrollment-tracker
outputs.desc: Tracker with submission dates, payer contacts, and status for each application

outputs.name: enrollment-issues
outputs.desc: Any rejections or requests for additional information

process: Submit the enrollment application to each target payer (portal, fax, or CAQH delegation).
Record the submission date and expected turnaround for each payer.
Follow up on applications at 30 and 60 days if no response.
Respond to payer requests for additional information within 48 hours.

steps.description: Record approvals and maintain the re-credentialing calendar.

outputs.name: credentialing-record
outputs.desc: Complete credentialing record with all payer participation dates and contract terms

outputs.name: recredentialing-calendar
outputs.desc: Calendar of upcoming re-credentialing dates and document expiration dates

process: Record the effective date and participation terms for each approved payer.
Set up the re-credentialing calendar (typically every 2 to 3 years per payer).
Track document expiration dates (licenses, malpractice insurance, DEA) and set renewal reminders.
Maintain the master credentialing file for audits and re-credentialing.

description: Report clinical quality measures for regulatory programs from measure identification through data collection, calculation, and submission.

steps.description: Identify the applicable quality reporting programs and measures for the practice.

inputs.name: practice-profile
inputs.desc: Practice type, specialty, payer mix, and provider count

inputs.name: reporting-year
inputs.desc: The calendar year for which quality measures are being reported

outputs.name: applicable-programs
outputs.desc: List of programs the practice must or should report to (MIPS, HEDIS, state programs)

outputs.name: selected-measures
outputs.desc: Specific measures selected for reporting, with definitions and data requirements

process: Identify mandatory programs based on practice size and payer participation (MIPS for Medicare, HEDIS for commercial).
Select the measures that align with the practice's specialty and patient population.
Review each measure's specifications (numerator, denominator, exclusions, data source).
Create the reporting timeline with submission deadlines.

steps.description: Collect the clinical data needed to calculate the selected quality measures.

inputs.name: selected-measures
inputs.desc: Measures with definitions and data requirements

outputs.name: measure-data
outputs.desc: Extracted clinical data organized by measure (eligible population, numerator events, exclusions)

outputs.name: data-quality-issues
outputs.desc: Data gaps or quality problems that could affect measure performance

process: Extract the eligible patient population for each measure from the EHR.
Identify the numerator events (patients who received the recommended care).
Apply the exclusion criteria.
Flag any data quality issues (missing documentation, incomplete records).

steps.description: Calculate the performance rates for each quality measure.

outputs.name: performance-rates
outputs.desc: Calculated performance rate for each measure (numerator/denominator, percentage, benchmark comparison)

outputs.name: improvement-opportunities
outputs.desc: Measures where performance is below benchmark, with root cause notes

process: Calculate the performance rate for each measure (numerator divided by denominator).
Compare the rates against national benchmarks and prior year performance.
Identify measures below the benchmark and investigate the root causes.
Document improvement opportunities for the quality improvement team.

steps.description: Submit the quality reports to the applicable programs and archive the documentation.

outputs.name: submission-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation of successful submission to each program with reference numbers

outputs.name: quality-reporting-record
outputs.desc: Complete quality reporting record for the year including data, calculations, and submissions

process: Format the data according to each program's submission specifications (QRDA, flat file, portal entry).
Submit the reports before the deadline for each program.
Verify the submission was accepted and record the confirmation.
Archive the complete reporting package for audit purposes.

description: Manage the practice revenue cycle end to end, from patient registration through final payment, with metrics monitoring and process improvement.

steps.description: Establish baseline metrics for the practice's revenue cycle performance.

inputs.name: practice-financial-data
inputs.desc: Billing data including charges, payments, adjustments, AR aging, and denial rates

inputs.name: reporting-period
inputs.desc: The time period to analyze (month, quarter, year)

outputs.name: baseline-metrics
outputs.desc: Key revenue cycle metrics: days in AR, clean claim rate, denial rate, collection rate, cost to collect

outputs.name: benchmark-comparison
outputs.desc: How the practice compares to industry benchmarks by specialty

process: Calculate days in accounts receivable (total AR divided by average daily charges).
Calculate the clean claim rate (claims accepted on first submission divided by total claims).
Calculate the denial rate (denied claims divided by total claims) and net collection rate.
Compare each metric against MGMA or specialty-specific benchmarks.

steps.description: Identify the bottlenecks in the revenue cycle that are reducing cash flow or increasing costs.

inputs.name: benchmark-comparison
inputs.desc: Gap between current performance and benchmarks

outputs.name: bottleneck-list
outputs.desc: Ranked list of revenue cycle bottlenecks with estimated financial impact

outputs.name: root-causes
outputs.desc: Root causes identified for each bottleneck

process: Analyze AR aging to identify where claims are stalling (0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ days).
Review denial reasons by category to find the highest-volume and highest-dollar denial types.
Examine the front-end processes (registration errors, insurance verification gaps, authorization delays).
Rank the bottlenecks by financial impact and fixability.

steps.description: Design and implement improvements to address the identified bottlenecks.

outputs.name: improvement-actions
outputs.desc: Specific actions to address each bottleneck, with owners, deadlines, and expected impact

outputs.name: monitoring-plan
outputs.desc: How to track whether the improvements are working

process: For each bottleneck, design a specific corrective action (training, process change, technology, staffing).
Assign an owner and deadline for each action.
Estimate the expected improvement in the target metric.
Define how progress will be measured (weekly AR review, monthly denial trending, quarterly collection rate).

steps.description: Produce the recurring revenue cycle report for practice leadership.

inputs.name: improvement-actions
inputs.desc: Actions in progress and their status

outputs.name: revenue-cycle-report
outputs.desc: Monthly report with current metrics, trend lines, improvement action status, and financial impact

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary of revenue cycle health for leadership

process: Pull the current month's metrics and compare to baseline and prior month.
Report the status of each improvement action (on track, delayed, completed).
Calculate the financial impact of completed improvements.
Produce the executive summary highlighting wins, risks, and next steps.

description: Set up a telehealth program for a medical practice, from platform selection through workflow configuration, payer verification, and launch.

steps.description: Evaluate and select a telehealth platform based on practice requirements.

inputs.name: practice-requirements
inputs.desc: Practice size, specialties, EHR system, and telehealth use cases

inputs.name: compliance-requirements
inputs.desc: HIPAA, state licensing, and payer requirements for telehealth

outputs.name: platform-selection
outputs.desc: Selected telehealth platform with rationale

outputs.name: platform-comparison
outputs.desc: Comparison of evaluated platforms on key criteria (EHR integration, cost, features, compliance)

process: Define the must-have features (EHR integration, scheduling, patient portal, mobile access, recording).
Evaluate platforms against the requirements (video quality, HIPAA compliance, cost, ease of use).
Check EHR integration compatibility and implementation effort.
Select the platform and document the rationale.

steps.description: Design the virtual visit workflow from scheduling through follow-up.

outputs.name: telehealth-workflow
outputs.desc: Step-by-step workflow for virtual visits (scheduling, intake, consent, visit, documentation, follow-up)

outputs.name: consent-forms
outputs.desc: Telehealth-specific consent forms for patient signature

process: Map the virtual visit workflow (scheduling, pre-visit tech check, intake, consent, video visit, post-visit).
Design the patient-facing process (how to join, what to prepare, technical requirements).
Create the telehealth consent form covering risks, limitations, and privacy.
Define the documentation requirements for telehealth visits.

steps.description: Verify payer coverage and reimbursement rules for telehealth visits.

outputs.name: payer-coverage-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix of payer coverage by visit type, CPT code, place of service, and modifier requirements

outputs.name: billing-guidelines
outputs.desc: Billing instructions for telehealth visits by payer

process: Check each major payer's telehealth coverage policies (covered visit types, originating site rules, provider types).
Identify the correct CPT codes, place of service codes, and modifiers for telehealth billing.
Verify state-specific telehealth regulations (licensure, prescribing, consent).
Build the payer coverage matrix and billing guidelines for the billing team.

steps.description: Train staff, launch the program, and monitor adoption and outcomes.

outputs.name: launch-checklist
outputs.desc: Completed launch checklist including training, testing, and go-live confirmation

outputs.name: telehealth-program-document
outputs.desc: Complete program documentation including workflow, billing, compliance, and monitoring plan

process: Train providers and staff on the platform, workflow, documentation, and billing.
Conduct test visits to verify the technology, workflow, and documentation.
Launch with a defined set of visit types and monitor volume, no-show rates, and patient satisfaction.
Review telehealth claim denials monthly and adjust billing practices as needed.
